name: xAI
legalName: X.AI Corp. — since February 2, 2026 a wholly-owned SpaceX subsidiary (combined entity branded 'SpaceXAI')
hq: Palo Alto, CA, USA (AI HQ); data centers Memphis, TN / Southaven, MS
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: xAI is the most aggressive self-builder in AI infrastructure — the Colossus campuses in Memphis/Southaven reached ~1.0 GW of nameplate compute draw by March 2026 (0 GW in 2023), built almost entirely on self-deployed behind-the-meter gas generation buffered by the world's largest Tesla Megapack installation — and it no longer exists as a standalone company: SpaceX acquired it February 2, 2026 (xAI valued ~$250B) and filed an IPO S-1 that makes its economics public for the first time: the AI segment lost $6.4B from operations on ~$3.2B revenue in 2025. BACKGROUND: Founded March 2023; acquired X in March 2025 ($80B/$33B); raised a $20B Series E at ~$230B (January 2026, NVIDIA and Cisco in) weeks before the SpaceX merger. Colossus 1: 100,000 H100s live in 122 days, now >220,000 GPUs. Colossus II: gigawatt-class (per SemiAnalysis, the first), with GB200/GB300 clusters brought up in 91 and 64 days. Monetization turned a corner in May 2026: Anthropic signed cloud agreements at $1.25B/month through May 2029 (~$15B/yr) for Colossus capacity. The unresolved liability: the gas fleet — up to 35 unpermitted mobile turbines documented at Memphis, 27 alleged at Southaven in a federal NAACP Clean Air Act suit ($399M litigation accrual), against a permitted path of 41 permanent turbines (1.2 GW plant) and mobile-unit removal by July 2027.
ecosystemRole: We assess xAI as the extreme case study in behind-the-fence power — the builder that proved gigawatt AI campuses can bypass the grid queue entirely, and the single largest battery-buffered AI deployment on earth. Basis: ~1.0 GW of compute powered 'almost entirely' by self-deployed generation (S-1), ~$731M of cumulative Tesla Megapack purchases smoothing GPU transients and enabling full grid-independence, and turbine procurement (~$3.7B of agreements in 2026 alone) that made xAI one of the largest mobile-turbine buyers anywhere. For power vendors, xAI defines both the opportunity (speed-at-any-cost procurement) and the risk template (permit litigation, community backlash, related-party procurement within the Musk complex). The Anthropic deal adds a second identity: Colossus is now also a merchant AI cloud.

productsAndServices.name: Colossus AI supercomputer campuses
productsAndServices.description: Colossus 1 (Memphis, former Electrolux site): 100,000 H100s in 122 days, doubled to 200,000 in 92 more; now >220,000 H100/H200/GB200 GPUs at ~130 MW+ compute. Colossus II (Memphis Tulane Rd + Southaven MS, defined in the S-1 as one coherent gigawatt-scale training cluster): ~110,000 GB200s (~210 MW) online in 91 days, 110,000 GB300s (220 MW) in 64 days, with >=220,000 more GB300s (>400 MW) next — designated for Grok 5 training. Combined ~1.0 GW nameplate compute draw; company claims >1M H100-equivalents across the fleet by end-2025.
productsAndServices.positioning: The fastest large-cluster builder on record (company-cited ~2-year industry benchmark for a 100 MW greenfield vs its 64-91-day cluster bring-ups); per-MW construction cost claimed 'considerably lower than industry benchmarks.'
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Historically internal (Grok training); now also merchant — the Anthropic cloud agreements at $1.25B/month through May 2029.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Musk targets: 1M GPUs at the Memphis facility by 2026; 50M H100-equivalents within 5 years; a next Memphis data center referencing up to 90 turbines; orbital compute framed as the strategic endgame (Anthropic reportedly interested in multi-GW orbital capacity).

productsAndServices.name: Behind-the-meter power stack (turbines + Megapacks)
productsAndServices.description: Self-designed, self-built generation: 69 temporary mobile turbines at Southaven (agreed removal August 2026 - July 2027 under a Mississippi DEQ order), a permitted 1.2 GW permanent 41-turbine gas plant under construction (Clean Air Act permit March 2026), SCR NOx controls on mobile units, plus the Stateline Power JV with Solaris Energy Infrastructure for off-grid supply. Turbine procurement 2026: $805M + $925M purchase agreements through 2029 plus a ~$2.0B mobile-turbine fleet acquisition. Buffering: >240 Megapacks at Colossus 1 alone — the S-1 claims the world's largest Megapack deployment and the first gigawatt-scale Megapack installation (2026) — enabling full off-grid operation during grid stress.
productsAndServices.positioning: The proof-of-concept for generation-plus-storage as the AI power architecture — and the sector's biggest related-party procurement story (Tesla Megapack purchases: $191M 2024, $506M 2025, $34M Q1 2026; another ~$269-295M by SpaceX in Q2 2026).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-consumed; Stateline Power JV (Solaris 50.1%/CTC 49.9%) rents equipment long-term.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Mobile-to-permanent transition through July 2027; grid supplements funded through MLGW/TVA partnerships (xAI pays network upgrades); $80M+ water recycling plant (~4.7B gallons/yr, ~9% aquifer-strain reduction).

productsAndServices.name: Grok models & the X platform (demand base)
productsAndServices.description: The Grok model line (Grok 3 through Grok 4.5, trained on tens of thousands of GB300s; Grok 5 in training), distributed through X (~550M combined MAUs; ~117M using Grok features), API/enterprise, and government channels (DoD $200M-ceiling frontier-AI contract; GSA $0.42/agency OneGov deal; reported classified-systems deployment). Terafab: a chip-manufacturing framework with Tesla and Intel targeting '1 TW/year of compute hardware' — agreed but not definitive.
productsAndServices.positioning: Third-to-fifth in consumer AI depending on metric (~15-18% US chatbot app share vs ChatGPT's ~45-53%); distribution via X, not model preference, drives adoption per press consensus.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: X subscriptions/ads, API, government contracts, and now wholesale compute (Anthropic).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Macrohard (agentic software platform with Tesla) in development; SpaceX IPO (reported ~$135/share, ~$75B raise) is the financing endgame.

recentDevelopments.headline: Anthropic signs cloud services agreements at $1.25B/month through May 2029 for Colossus capacity
recentDevelopments.read: The single most important commercial event in xAI's history — ~$15B/yr of contracted compute revenue against an AI segment that booked $3.2B in all of 2025. Colossus stops being a cost center and becomes a merchant cloud; the 90-day termination right is the caveat. The same announcement floated Anthropic interest in 'multiple gigawatts' of orbital compute.

recentDevelopments.headline: SpaceX S-1 goes public — AI segment lost $6.4B from operations on ~$3.2B revenue in 2025
recentDevelopments.read: First filing-grade look at xAI economics: segment operating losses of $1.56B (2024), $6.36B (2025), $2.47B (Q1 2026 alone), with Nameplate Compute Draw disclosed as a KPI (0→1.0 GW in 3 years). The IPO (reported ~$135/share, ~$75B raise) is the financing mechanism for the whole buildout.

recentDevelopments.headline: ~$2.0B mobile gas turbine fleet acquisition; $805M + $925M turbine purchase agreements through 2029 signed earlier in 2026
recentDevelopments.read: ~$3.7B of turbine commitments in four months makes xAI one of the largest mobile-turbine buyers anywhere — a demand shock in a market where every AIDC developer is chasing the same units. Bridge strategy: mobile units carry load until the permitted 1.2 GW permanent plant completes.

recentDevelopments.headline: NAACP/SELC file federal Clean Air Act suit over 27 allegedly unpermitted Southaven turbines; xAI records $399M litigation accrual
recentDevelopments.read: The sector's defining environmental-justice case. Turbine counts by evidentiary status: 35 documented at Memphis (33 thermal-imaged operating), 15 permitted backup-only by Shelby County, 27 alleged at Southaven in the federal complaint, 41 permitted by MDEQ (March 2026). The $399M accrual says the company itself prices real exposure. Every behind-the-meter developer's permitting playbook is now shaped by this case.

recentDevelopments.headline: SpaceX acquires xAI (~$250B) — combined 'SpaceXAI' at ~$1.25T files for IPO
recentDevelopments.read: Largest M&A deal ever reported; solves xAI's funding problem by attaching a $6B+/yr cash burn to SpaceX's balance sheet and IPO proceeds. Common-control accounting, no public independent fairness process — the related-party pattern (Tesla Megapacks, X data, Musk on all sides) is now a disclosed risk factor rather than a rumor.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series E closes at $20B raised, ~$230B valuation — NVIDIA and Cisco among strategic investors
recentDevelopments.read: Upsized from a $15B target; NVIDIA investing in its own largest merchant GPU buyer continues the circular-financing pattern visible across the AI buildout (cf. NVIDIA-OpenAI, NVIDIA-CoreWeave). Four weeks later the SpaceX merger made the round look like a bridge.

recentDevelopments.headline: Clean Air Act permit granted for permanent 1.2 GW, 41-turbine behind-the-meter gas plant at Southaven
recentDevelopments.read: The permitted endgame for Colossus II power: mobile units out by July 2027 under the MDEQ agreed order, permanent plant in. S-1 language confirms the campus 'is capable of operating entirely' off self-built generation — the grid becomes the supplement, not the source.

recentDevelopments.headline: Colossus II clusters brought online at record pace — 110,000 GB200s in 91 days, 110,000 GB300s in 64 days
recentDevelopments.read: SemiAnalysis independently called Colossus II the first gigawatt-scale coherent training cluster, with ~460 MW of on-site gas generation documented across the two campuses. Fleet ended 2025 above 1M H100-equivalents (company claim). Build velocity — not model quality — is xAI's clearest verified edge.

recentDevelopments.headline: DoD awards xAI a $200M-ceiling frontier-AI contract; GSA OneGov deal follows at $0.42/agency
recentDevelopments.read: Government traction despite the July 2025 Grok conduct incidents (which drew a Warren letter questioning the award). Axios later reported Grok deployment into classified systems (Feb 2026). Grok's antisemitic-output episode remains a live procurement-risk flag.

recentDevelopments.headline: Executive churn: co-founder Igor Babuschkin, CFO Mike Liberatore (after ~3 months), and GC Robert Keele all exit in 2025
recentDevelopments.read: Babuschkin left to found an AI-safety VC — read by press as a safety-culture signal. The xAI-v.-OpenAI trade-secrets suit that followed the departures has been dismissed twice. Post-merger, the executive layer is SpaceX's (Musk/Shotwell/Johnsen); xAI-specific leadership is no longer separately disclosed.

strategyRead: (High confidence) xAI's core differentiator is speed-to-power, not model quality — behind-the-meter gas plus Megapack buffering lets it bypass multi-year interconnection queues entirely, and its 64-91-day cluster bring-ups are the fastest independently corroborated in the industry. Basis: S-1 KPI disclosures (0→1.0 GW nameplate compute draw in 3 years), SemiAnalysis technical verification of the gigawatt-scale coherent cluster, and TVA/MLGW grid allocations (~300 MW) covering only a fraction of campus load.

(High confidence) For power and storage vendors, xAI is simultaneously the best demand signal and the worst-risk template in AIDC. Basis: ~$3.7B of 2026 turbine commitments and ~$1B cumulative Megapack purchases prove procurement velocity; the NAACP federal suit, four different turbine counts with different evidentiary statuses, and a $399M self-recorded accrual prove the permitting and community-relations downside of the same playbook.

(Moderate confidence) The Anthropic deal (~$15B/yr) converts Colossus into a merchant cloud and roughly quintuples segment revenue run-rate — but concentration and the 90-day termination right make it fragile. We assess xAI's economics remain IPO-dependent: even at full Anthropic ramp, capex (+$9.6B in 2025, +$6.0B in Q1 2026 alone) outruns contracted revenue. Basis: S-1 figures; the ~$75B raise target is press-reported.

(Moderate confidence) Related-party procurement is structural, not incidental: Tesla Megapacks (~$731M-1B cumulative, figures vary by source), Tesla's equity stake, X data feeding Grok, and the common-control SpaceX merger with no publicly detailed fairness process. Vendors negotiating with SpaceXAI should assume Tesla gets first look at any storage scope. Basis: S-1 related-party disclosures, Tesla filings, CNBC/Electrek reporting.

(Low confidence) Combined-fleet claims beyond verified figures — 555,000+ GPUs / ~2 GW combined (Introl tracker), 1M GPUs at Memphis by end-2026, 50M H100-equivalents in 5 years, orbital gigawatts, and the 'Terafab' 1 TW/yr chip fab with Tesla and Intel — rest on Musk statements and industry trackers, not tier-1 verification. Treat as directional ambition, not plan-of-record.

specs: Combined nameplate compute draw: ~1.0 GW (March 31, 2026); trajectory 0 GW (2023) → 0.3 GW (2024) → 0.8 GW (2025) → 1.0 GW
Colossus 1: ~100,000 H100s / ~130 MW in 122 days (workloads 19 days after first server delivery); doubled to 200,000 GPUs in 92 days; now >220,000 H100/H200/GB200
Colossus II: ~110,000 GB200s (~210 MW) in 91 days; 110,000 GB300s (220 MW) in 64 days; next phase ≥220,000 GB300s (>400 MW) for Grok 5 training
Cooling: advanced direct-to-chip liquid cooling for high rack density; brownfield retrofits of industrial shells
Grid: TVA-approved 2×150 MW allocations (Memphis); Southaven campus in MISO territory on the former 640 MW Duke Energy plant site
Permitted permanent plant: 1.2 GW / 41 turbines at Southaven (Clean Air Act permit March 2026), under construction

Mobile fleet: 69 temporary turbines at Southaven under MDEQ agreed order (removal Aug 2026 - Jul 2027); SemiAnalysis documented ~460 MW on-site gas across both campuses (12 SMT-130s Memphis; 7 Titan 350s Southaven)
SCR NOx controls on mobile units; SELC estimated 1,200-2,000 tons/yr NOx from the unpermitted Memphis fleet at its peak
Storage: >240 Megapacks at Colossus 1; S-1 claims world's largest Megapack deployment and first gigawatt-scale Megapack installation (2026); enables full off-grid operation
Water: $80M+ recycle plant, ~4.745B gallons/yr, ~9% Memphis Aquifer strain reduction
